doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Composing for goals: the 2004 Lincoln Center commission
summary: Fingers-first ideas versus commissions, including the Let Freedom Swing piece co-composed with Zim Ngqawana.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When you sit down to write if you have a goal, a specific goal in mind of — you wrote a song for his 80th birthday and you wrote something performed at Lincoln Center, do you approach this composition work differently than if you’re just — you’re in the mood to write, you sit and wait for something to happen. Is there a different approach depending on the goal?

Oh absolutely. There’s — look in terms of waiting for something to happen if I just come up with a phrase when I’m practicing — some things don’t come from the brain, they come from the fingers you know. And it won’t be — in my case — I’m not that brilliant that it will be complete but it will be enough to say gosh you know if I develop this, if I extend it, if I, you know, you would know all the manipulations that are possible you know I’ve actually got something. That’s one thing. If I’m — and then you referred to Commission 2004, which was — we mentioned his name earlier with Zim Ngqawana — we co-composed it. That was for the opening of Rose Hall at Lincoln Center and it was part of a series, “Let Freedom Swing.” And for your kind of footnoting you should Google that. But that had commissions for me and Zim, for Toshiko, for was it Jimmy Heath maybe. And there were a series of commissions for that week which preceded that election — it was also an election year, interestingly. And it was kind of — my commission was settings they had already selected them, of quotations from Nelson © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

Mandela and Archbishop Desmond Tutu. All of the other commissions were also musical settings from speeches — oh Billy Childs was another one. But anyway, get the facts because it’s fascinating. I don’t want to be responsible in this interview for naming everyone and getting everything exact.
